back_translation: In that day the LORD will punish Leviathan the fleeing serpent and Leviathan the coiling, twisting serpent with His sword — sharp, great, and mighty — and He will slay the dragon of the sea.
In that day: "Sing antiphonally about the delightful vineyard.
I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it every moment. I guard and protect it night and day, so that no one can harm it.
I have no wrath remaining. If only thorns and briers would confront Me in battle — I would march in and trample them; I would burn them all completely.
Or else let him take hold of My strong shelter; let him make peace with Me — let him make peace with Me."
In days to come, Jacob will take root; Israel will bud and blossom, and his fruit will fill the face of the whole world.
Has He struck Israel as He struck the one who struck him? Was Israel slain as his slayers were slain?
You contended with her in due measure, by driving her away — He swept her out with His fierce wind, as on the day the east wind blows.

Therefore by this Jacob's guilt will be atoned for, and this will be the full fruit of the removal of his sin: when he makes all the altar stones like white chalkstone crushed to pieces, no Asherah poles or incense altars will be left standing.
For the fortified city stands desolate and alone, a dwelling forsaken and abandoned like the wilderness. There the calf grazes; there it lies down and strips its branches bare.

When its branches are dry, they are broken off; women come and take them to kindle fires. For this is a nation without understanding; therefore their Maker will not have compassion on them, and their Former will show them no favor.
And in that day the LORD will thresh out the grain, from the flowing River Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt, and you, O sons of Israel, will be gathered and gleaned one by one.

And in that day a great ram's horn will be blown, and those who were perishing in the land of Assyria and those driven out to the land of Egypt will come back, and they will worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
